claims.head: The Oilers’ power play outclasses the Kings’
claims.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, at the lethal end; the Kings are near the bottom of the league, at the harmless end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Oilers and the Kings sit at opposite ends for power play.
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more per 60 than the Kings’.

claims.head: Good looks against hopeful ones
claims.body: The Oilers are around the middle of the league for shot quality, at the dangerous end; the Kings are one of the league’s worst, at the hopeful end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Oilers and the Kings sit at opposite ends for shot quality.
claims.call: The Oilers’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Kings’.

notes.text: Z. Hyman has been a scratch for the last 4 games. He is a top-six forward.
R. Nugent-Hopkins is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
M. Savoie is out another eight weeks (lower body injury) and has not played this season. L. Draisaitl has taken his spot beside C. McDavid and V. Podkolzin.
F. Hallander joined from PIT on Oct 7 and has played beside J. Dickinson and K. Kapanen.
K. Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 57% of the team’s power-play time in 5 games, up from 6% last season.
T. Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 30% last season.
M. Zuccarello is out week to week, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

LAK.head: A tough matchup for Los Angeles
LAK.body: Edmonton has had more of the chances over recent games, Edmonton will be without Hyman, and Los Angeles has home ice. Los Angeles can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

EDM.head: Edmonton has a lot going for them
